equity_bridge.item: Pension and post-retirement underfunding, after tax

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mature global tools market low-single-digit volume plus price; every trailing CAGR is distorted by M&A (Craftsman, MTD, Excel), divestitures (Security 2022, Infrastructure 2024, CAM 2026) and the FY2022-23 destock collapse
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs (-2.3% / -3.9%) diverge >30% from revenue (-3.7% / +3.5%) and EPS (-27.9% / -19.5%). Equity shrank on FY2023 losses and dividends paid out of a depressed earnings base; EPS CAGRs run from a peak (FY2020 7.85, FY2021 10.55) into a trough (FY2025 2.66). None is a usable forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not deducted: net debt company). Owner FCF: FY2020 1,564.9; FY2021 25.7; FY2022 -2,080.6; FY2023 768.8; FY2024 647.6; FY2025 593.8. The 3-yr CAGR is undefined (negative start). SBC is ~0.6% of revenue and is not growing faster than cash flow; the FCF decline is margin and working capital, not dilution.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation, not peak or trough extrapolation. The completed ~$2.1B cost programme and the China-to-North-America sourcing shift carry gross margin to the guided 34-35% in H2 2026 and ~34% thereafter, but SWK keeps reinvesting in SG&A and the tariff regime leaves a cost floor that did not exist pre-2022, so EBITDA settles at 14% -- about 1pp below the FY2015-21 average on the same definition. Revenue grows 2-3.5% from a pro forma ex-CAM base: modest housing/DIY recovery from 2027 plus price, with DEWALT holding but not regaining professional cordless share from Milwaukee.
scenario_narratives.bull: The cost-out meets a demand recovery. Lower mortgage rates revive housing turnover and repair/remodel, outdoor and DIY volumes recover to the pre-2022 trend, and operating leverage on the leaner cost base returns EBITDA to the ~15.5% pre-2022 mid-cycle. Tariff mitigation completes, price sticks, and DEWALT innovation stops the share bleed to Techtronic. Requires several independent things to go right.
scenario_narratives.bear: The trough is structural. Tariff-driven price increases meet elastic DIY demand into a consumer slowdown, revenue falls in 2027, new trade actions overwhelm the mitigation plan, and Milwaukee keeps winning the professional cordless platform war. EBITDA stalls at ~11.5%, close to FY2024-26 levels, and the narrower post-divestiture portfolio is more housing-concentrated than before.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SWK is valued on a mid-cycle owner-FCF basis because its last five years span a peak (FY2021), a working-capital and margin collapse (FY2022-23, negative owner FCF) and a slow cost-programme-led recovery (FY2024-26). Extrapolating FY2025 (~4% owner-FCF margin) would undervalue a business with ~$2.1B of completed cost-out; extrapolating FY2019-21 (~15% EBITDA, then-larger portfolio) would ignore Milwaukee share loss and the tariff cost floor. The base case lets margins recover over four years to ~1pp below the old mid-cycle and caps the terminal value at 13x FCF, the cyclical-industrial band.
key_risks_to_valuation: Tariff policy: a further escalation could overwhelm pricing and reshoring mitigation; Q2 2026 gross margin included ~250bp of non-repeatable tariff-refund benefit
Professional cordless share loss to Techtronic/Milwaukee caps both price and volume in DEWALT
US housing/DIY demand stays depressed by mortgage rates for longer
Leverage ~2.5x net debt/EBITDA plus off-balance-sheet receivables factoring; the 58-year dividend streak competes with deleveraging for cash
Pro forma base revenue depends on an ESTIMATED CAM revenue carve-out and 53rd-week adjustment (~$530M combined); a $300M error in the base is ~$2/share

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 61.90-104.68
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 93556) for FY2023-25 10-K and Q1/Q2 2026 10-Q: revenue, COGS, SG&A, depreciation, amortisation, SBC, capex, OCF, debt, cash, CP, divestiture proceeds, diluted shares, cover-page shares; SWK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics for the FY2007-25 history and KPIs (cash taxes, interest income, buybacks)
data_sources.qualitative: SWK_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): segments, Q2 2026 results, FY2026 guidance (adj EPS $5.20-5.80, FCF $600-800M, H2 adj GM 34-35%, ~$800M gross tariff cost), bull/bear points

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation 94.1M). Tax withheld on net-share settlement is not XBRL-tagged and is immaterial for SWK (low-teens $M historically); no combined figure published, so the add-back alone is used.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 151.02M basic shares on the 10-Q cover (dei, 2026-07-24) + 0.52M dilutive-securities adjustment (Q2 2026 10-Q) = ~151.5M. Q2 2026 weighted diluted was 150.6M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. SWK resumed buybacks in Q2 2026 ($252.1M, funded by CAM proceeds), so the flat count is being paid for rather than a modelling convention; FY2023-25 buybacks were only $16-20M/yr.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Saturday nearest 31 December (52/53-week; FY2025 ended 2026-01-03 and was a 53-week year)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.25 (cyclical, housing-linked, 2.5x levered) -> cost of equity ~10.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (4.2% after tax). Market D/V ~24% (net debt $4.2B vs market cap ~$13.6B). WACC ~9.0%, identical across scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost is already inside COGS/SG&A and therefore inside the EBITDA margin; operating lease liabilities ($453.6M at 2026-07-04) are EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment (B-equivalent), lease_cost_pct_path 0.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing: US operating company, cyclical industrial/consumer tools -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations for cyclical risk-once, WC sign and lease treatment). Not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco; no live corporate action for the whole company. First valuation of SWK (no memory entry, no prior DCF). MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION: neither the latest year nor the peak is extrapolated. FY2025 sits in a margin trough (GAAP gross margin 30.3%, EBITDA on the definition below ~10.6%) after the FY2022-23 destock/inflation collapse (FY2023 ~6.9%, owner FCF negative in FY2021-22); FY2015-21 ran ~15% on the same definition with gross margin 33-35%. Base recovers to 14.0% by Y5 (~1pp below the pre-2022 mid-cycle, haircut for Milwaukee share loss, a structural tariff cost floor and permanent SG&A reinvestment); bull 15.5%, bear stalls at 11.5%. EBITDA DEFINITION used in the margin paths: gross profit - SG&A + depreciation (365.6M FY2025; intangible amortisation sits in 'Other, net' so it is NOT added back) + SBC (to make it pre-SBC, SBC is charged separately) - ~0.8pp of revenue for recurring restructuring/other charges, which SWK incurs every year and an owner must pay. FY2025 = 10.6%, H1 2026 ~10.4%, Q2 2026 ~11.5% (flattered by ~250bp of net tariff-refund benefit in gross margin, not repeatable). BASE REVENUE: FY2025 15,130.4 less ~250 for the 53rd week and ~280 of CAM revenue (CAM sold to the buyer for $1.8B; $1,814.7M proceeds and a $273.7M gain booked in Q2 2026; CAM annual revenue ~$400M+ is an estimate, not disclosed in XBRL) -> ~14,600 pro forma, 52-week, continuing portfolio. Y1 growth (FY2026) of 2% reflects H1 2026 organic +~3% and HSD US T&O price increases offset by soft DIY/outdoor volume. NET DEBT: long-term debt 4,757.9 (includes 53.7 current portion) + commercial paper 0.0 at 2026-07-04, less cash 592.4 = 4,165.5. The DB/CSV total_debt (4,811.6) double-counts the current portion (same XBRL pattern as KEYS/NDSN) and is not used. Interest income (~$150M/yr run-rate, largely swap/financing-related) is NOT a cash pile's yield -- SWK carries net debt -- so interest_income is 0 in the owner-FCF base and the flows are unlevered (all interest excluded, net debt subtracted once). Receivables-sale (factoring) programs are not added to debt; flagged as a modest understatement of leverage. WC capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of the revenue change): inventory 3.9B + receivables 1.2B >> payables 2.4B, so growth consumes cash. The FY2026 inventory release that supports the $600-800M FCF guidance is deliberately not capitalised. DATA QUALITY: in Metrics.csv/core_metrics the 2026 quarter labels are shifted one quarter late -- the row labelled 'Q2 2026' is fiscal Q1 2026 (ended 2026-04-04) and 'Q3 2026' is fiscal Q2 2026 (ended 2026-07-04); the XBRL fp/fy tags on the 2025-26 10-Qs are mislabelled (Q2 2025 10-Q tagged fy 2026). Q3 2026 has not been reported (due late Oct).

bear.narrative: Price elasticity on the HSD tariff increases plus a 2027 consumer slowdown cut volume; new trade actions push the gross tariff cost above the $800M mitigation plan; Milwaukee keeps taking professional cordless share, so the margin recovery stalls at ~11.5% EBITDA -- the FY2024-26 trough becomes the new normal. Leverage (~2.5x) stays sticky and capital goes to the dividend and debt, not growth.

base.narrative: Gross margin reaches the guided 34-35% band in H2 2026 and holds ~34% thereafter (tariff refunds fade, China-sourcing <5% and footprint savings stick); SG&A stays elevated at ~21-22% as the $300M+ commercial reinvestment continues; EBITDA 14% by FY2030 versus ~15% pre-2022. Housing/DIY recovers slowly from 2027; DEWALT holds share against Milwaukee but does not take it back.

bull.narrative: Rate cuts unlock a US housing turnover and repair/remodel upcycle from 2027; volume leverage on the post-$2.1B-programme cost base pushes gross margin to 35-36% and EBITDA back to the 15.5% pre-2022 mid-cycle; tariff policy stabilises with pricing retained; DEWALT innovation halts the professional-cordless share loss.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a cyclical with ~2.5x net debt/EBITDA, a live tariff-policy dependency (~$800M gross 2026 cost) and documented share loss in its most important category. Base 50%: the cost programme is complete and H1 2026 margins are tracking guidance. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs a housing recovery, tariff stability and a halt to share loss simultaneously.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
